simple.meaning: יָקוּשׁ (yâqûwsh) is a Hebrew word meaning “properly, entangled , i.e. by implication (intransitively) a snare , or (transitive) a snarer.” BibleIQ connects the English word back to this source word so its use can be compared across Scripture.
simple.biblicalBackground: יָקוּשׁ (H3353) appears 3 times in the Hebrew Bible, beginning at Psalms 91:3, with occurrences in Psalms, Proverbs, Jeremiah.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to יָקוּשׁ (H3353) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: English translations can use the same English word for different Hebrew words. BibleIQ anchors the study in יָקוּשׁ (H3353) before moving outward to related references.
simple.summary: יָקוּשׁ (yâqûwsh) / H3353 is traced through Psalms 91:3, Proverbs 6:5, Jeremiah 5:26 using source-language evidence and occurrence comparison.

definitions.short: properly, entangled , i.e. by implication (intransitively) a snare , or (transitive) a snarer
definitions.full: H3353. yaqush יָקוּשׁ noun [masculine] id.; יָקוּשׁ מַּח Psa 91:3 ; יָקוּשׁ מִיַּד כְּצִמּוֺר Prov 6:5 ; plural יְקוּשִׁים Jer 5:26 (in simile)

occurrences.englishText: For he will deliver you from the snare of the fowler,
Free yourself, like a gazelle from the hand of the hunter,
For wicked men are found among my people. They watch, as fowlers lie in wait. They set a trap. They catch men.
